findings.title: Error handling test has inverted assertion
findings.body: In `test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling`, the docstring says 'Test that errors in processing don't block offset commits for other messages', but the assertion `assert len(committed_offsets) == 0 or test_partition not in committed_offsets` expects the opposite: that no commits happen. The `OrderedQueueWorker.run` calls `self.offset_tracker.complete_offset(...)` in a `finally` block, so offsets are always marked complete regardless of whether `result_processor` raised. The `OffsetTracker.get_committable_offsets` would then return offset 101 (the highest contiguous completed), and the wrapped `commit_offsets` would commit `{partition: 102}` to Kafka via `track_commits`. The assertion would fail on a correct implementation. The test should instead assert `test_partition in committed_offsets` (or similar) to verify that errors don't block commits.

findings.title: Per-item metrics gauge in worker hot loop
findings.body: In `OrderedQueueWorker.run`, the `finally` block calls `metrics.gauge('remote_subscriptions.queue_worker.queue_depth', self.work_queue.qsize(), tags={'identifier': self.identifier})` for every processed work item. For a high-throughput uptime results consumer, this emits one metrics sample per processed message, flooding the metrics pipeline. Queue depth should be reported periodically (e.g., from `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.poll()`, which already emits `remote_subscriptions.queue_pool.total_queued`), not per-item.

findings.title: OffsetTracker lock initialization relies on CPython dict atomicity
findings.body: `_get_partition_lock` uses a check-then-set pattern (`self.partition_locks.get(partition)` followed by `self.partition_locks.setdefault(...)`). While `dict.setdefault` is atomic under CPython's GIL, this is not guaranteed by the language and could create duplicate `Lock` instances for the same partition on alternative Python implementations (PyPy, Jython, etc.), causing concurrent `add_offset`/`complete_offset` calls on the same partition to operate on different locks and corrupt the `all_offsets`/`outstanding` sets. A single initialization lock or `defaultdict(threading.Lock)` would be safer and clearer.

findings.title: Kafka integration test reaches into arroyo internals
findings.body: `test_thread_queue_parallel_kafka_offset_commit` calls `processor._run_once()` and `processor._shutdown()` to drive the `StreamProcessor`. Both methods are underscore-prefixed private APIs of the `arroyo` library and are not part of any documented contract; future arroyo releases can rename/remove them without warning and silently break this test. The test should either use the public `run()`/`shutdown()` API or be marked as expected to fail on arroyo upgrades.

findings.title: ResultsStrategyFactory.shutdown leaks multiprocessing pool
findings.body: `shutdown()` releases `parallel_executor` and (newly added) `queue_pool`, but never calls `self.multiprocessing_pool.shutdown()`. When mode is `parallel`, the `MultiprocessingPool` (with worker processes spawned from `multiprocessing.cpu_count()`) is left running until process exit. This is a pre-existing bug, but the PR adds a sibling `queue_pool` cleanup and is the natural place to fix it.

findings.title: hash()-based group assignment is not stable across restarts
findings.body: `get_queue_for_group` uses the built-in `hash(group_key) % self.num_queues`. Python randomizes string hashes per process (`PYTHONHASHSEED`), meaning the same `subscription_id` may map to a different queue index after a consumer restart. Within a single process order is preserved per queue, and Kafka offset commits ensure reprocessing starts from the right offset, so the risk of out-of-order processing is low. Flagging because `hash()` for routing is a common source of subtle ordering bugs and `hashlib` or a stable scheme (e.g., `zlib.crc32`) would be safer; reviewers should confirm this is acceptable.

findings.title: Commit/mark_committed window can re-commit same offsets
findings.body: In `_commit_loop`, `self.commit_function(committable)` is called before `mark_committed` updates `last_committed`. If a later step in the same iteration raises (or the commit is slow and another `_commit_loop` tick observes the same state on the next second), `get_committable_offsets` can return the same offset set again and `commit_function` will be called twice with the same data. Kafka offset commits are idempotent so this is not a correctness bug, but the lack of atomicity between commit and state update means a duplicate commit is possible; holding a lock across both calls, or marking committed before invoking the commit function with a rollback on failure, would be cleaner.

findings.title: worker.shutdown flag is redundant with queue.shutdown
findings.body: `FixedQueuePool.shutdown` sets `worker.shutdown = True` and then calls `q.shutdown(immediate=False)`. The worker loop checks `self.shutdown` only at the top, but is blocked in `work_queue.get()`, so the flag has no effect until the queue is drained. After `q.shutdown(immediate=False)`, `get()` raises `queue.ShutDown` once the queue is empty, so the flag is dead. Removing it (or documenting why both are needed) would make the intent clearer.
